description: This walk takes you along a section of the Wales Coast Path from Bracelet Bay to Langland Bay and Caswell Bay. The route runs for just under 3 miles, starting from the parking area between Bracelet Bay and Limeslade Bay. The walk explores the eastern edge of the Gower Peninsula, following the cliffs and headlands around Mumbles towards some of the area's most popular beaches. The route offers excellent views across Swansea Bay, with rocky shorelines, grassy cliff tops and a series of sheltered bays along the way.Starting near Bracelet Bay, the path passes close to the distinctive Mumbles Head, with its historic lighthouse standing offshore on the headland. The route then continues past Limeslade Bay before reachingLangland Bay, a popular sandy beach backed by cliffs and colourful beach huts. Continuing along the coast, you arrive atCaswell Bay, a wide sandy beach with rock pools, coastal walks and views along the Gower coastline.The coastline around Bracelet Bay, Langland Bay and Caswell Bay is a great place for spotting seabirds, while seals and dolphins are occasionally seen from the cliffs. The nearby village of Mumbles has a wide range of cafés, restaurants and independent shops, as well as attractions including Mumbles Pier and the Victorian promenade.
